transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Halcyon Head of ML), Ravi Menon (Halcyon Infra), Lena Ortiz (Halcyon CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on latency/throughput requirements for a customer-facing chat assistant. Discussed p95 SLO targets, concurrency, streaming behavior and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Agreed next steps to run benchmark with sample prompts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, and Carlos our systems eng is here as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Jenna Park: good, thanks, uh excited to dig in, we've been tracking Redwood's performance benchmarks and wanted to validate on our workload.
[00:12] Carlos Vega: great, quick intro from me — I run performance and infra for Redwood's runtime, happy to go deep on streaming and token/sec.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: hey all — I'm Lena, CTO. main thing for us is tail latency, we have customer SLA of p95 200ms for chat responses, ideally <150ms for premium tier.
[00:29] Ravi Menon: hey, I'm Ravi — infra. want to understand network hops for VPC and if private deployment is required for data residency.
[00:36] Maya Thompson: perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. quick qualification: what models are you currently using?
[00:41] Jenna Park: mostly a fine-tuned open Llama derivative for chat, 8k context, we stream tokens back to the client. average output length is 60-120 tokens, bursts up to 400 tokens for long summaries. concurrency expected about 8-12 active users in peak, with occasional spikes to 40.
[01:00] Carlos Vega: ok, good context. streaming changes the math — p95 streaming latency typically measured to first token or to full response?
[01:07] Lena Ortiz: first token is most important for perceived latency, but we also care about end-to-end for billing and timeouts.
[01:13] Carlos Vega: understood. so target p95 first-token 150ms at 8 concurrent streaming sessions, and tail for end-to-end under 800ms for the typical 60-120 token responses sounds reasonable. question: are you open to Dedicated GPU pools for consistent throughput or do you prefer Hosted?
[01:30] Jenna Park: we prefer Hosted for ease initially, but if Dedicated is required to meet p95 at scale we'd consider it. also private/VPC is on the table for compliance.
[01:38] Maya Thompson: great — we usually run a short benchmark with your sample prompts to validate. our benchmark measures: p50/p95/p99 first token, tokens/sec while streaming, concurrency throughput (requests/sec) and GPU util.
[01:50] Ravi Menon: what's a realistic token/sec we should expect? our UI streams so we care about both steady-state token/sec and prefix costs.
[01:57] Carlos Vega: depends on model size and quantization. for a 7B-style quantized model on our Dedicated pool you might see 40-80 tokens/sec per stream for generation; smaller models faster, larger models slower. for first token we optimize kernel selection and KV cache to drop p95. sometimes transcriptions show KV cache as KV cash — just a note, the infra detail matters.
[02:18] Jenna Park: we do quantize to int8 in-house for cost reasons; are there gotchas with that?
[02:22] Carlos Vega: int8 quantization is supported — key tradeoffs: slight quality delta, larger variance in p99 if you push batch sizes too far. for streaming and low-latency, we keep batch sizes small and rely on continuous batching and prefix caching.
[02:35] Maya Thompson: Jenna, when you say bursts to 40 concurrent, is that sustained or short spiky traffic?
[02:40] Jenna Park: mostly short spikes, like 2-3 minutes during promotions.
[02:44] Carlos Vega: ok, that's where Dedicated with burst capacity or hosted with routing policies comes in. we can set autoscale to add warm workers, and we do automated fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained.
[02:56] Ravi Menon: curious about SaaS Hosted vs Dedicated predictability — how deterministic are p95 numbers on Hosted?
[03:03] Carlos Vega: Hosted has more variability — we expose performance profiles per model, but for strict SLOs Dedicated is recommended; you get reserved GPU pools and stronger latencies. Hosted is great for early phases.
[03:13] Lena Ortiz: for private deployments, what's the integration surface for KMS/auditing? we run an HSM for keys.
[03:19] Maya Thompson: our Private option supports customer-managed KMS integrations and audit logs; we can ship an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements. we'll share SOC2 and VPC network checklists.
[03:29] Jenna Park: awesome. can you share typical numbers for p95 first-token for streaming on Dedicated with 8 concurrent on a 7B model?
[03:36] Carlos Vega: ballpark: p95 first token around 80-160ms depending on batch strategy, kernel path, and sequence length. with an optimized runtime and prefix caching we've seen p95 ~90ms for many workloads.
[03:46] Maya Thompson: and we can run a benchmark with your exact prompts to validate. our benchmark tool will produce charts per-token latency, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
[03:54] Ravi Menon: are there network requirements for VPC peering? NAT/gateway, firewall rules — we need specifics for private deployment.
[04:01] Carlos Vega: yes, we'll provide a network checklist: whitelisted IP ranges, peering instructions, MTU recommendations, and an expected egress encryption handshake.
[04:08] Jenna Park: what about streaming token/sec during long responses (300-400 tokens)? will that push p95 out?
[04:14] Carlos Vega: not directly for first token, but end-to-end increases. we optimize by streaming early tokens as soon as they are generated — continuous decoding and sending. token/sec steady-state can be 30-60 tps; GPUs have micro-batching that increases throughput without large latency penalty if configured correctly.
[04:31] Maya Thompson: quick note — some of our customers measure p95 to first content byte and others to full completion; we'll match your metric in the benchmark.
[04:39] Lena Ortiz: what about concurrency measured vs sessions? we have some long-lived open websockets and others are short-lived HTTP calls.
[04:45] Carlos Vega: websockets for streaming are fine; we size worker processes by concurrent streams. long-lived sessions use more memory due to KV cache per session, so there is a memory vs concurrency tradeoff. we can share suggested memory/GPU configs.
[04:59] Jenna Park: can you do a quick walkthrough of the benchmark steps?
[05:02] Maya Thompson: yeah — step 1: Halcyon provides prompt set and expected distribution of response lengths. step 2: Redwood runs benchmark in a non-prod Dedicated pool or Hosted sandbox, measuring p50/p95/p99 first-token and full response, tokens/sec, GPU util, and tail events. step 3: we review results and iterate on batching, quantization and routing. final step: if Dedicated/Private required, we scope Dedicated sizing and pricing.
[05:23] Ravi Menon: how long does the benchmark take?
[05:26] Carlos Vega: a representative 2-hour run usually surfaces tail issues, but we can do a 30-minute smoke first.
[05:31] Jenna Park: what's the expected cost for that run? (laugh)
[05:34] Maya Thompson: we can include a credit for one benchmark run as part of the POC — we'll call that out in pricing.
[05:39] Lena Ortiz: any common surprises you see in these evaluations?
[05:42] Carlos Vega: yes — often the token distribution is heavier than expected, causing higher average GPU memory and occasional p99 spikes. also network serialization and small-batch inefficiencies can cause first-token jitter.
[05:54] Jenna Park: do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs? we rely on some tool-calling patterns which affect prompt format and tokens/sec.
[06:01] Maya Thompson: yes — Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output; we'll include guidance on how that impacts tokens and latency.
[06:07] Ravi Menon: security question — how is logs retention handled for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[06:12] Maya Thompson: Hosted stores logs per our retention policy; Dedicated gives configurable retention and VPC/private gives customer control — we can do zero retention for sensitive data on Private. we'll share the options.
[06:22] Carlos Vega: another performance note: quantization and kernel selection can change determinism in tail latency; our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles per workload to balance cost and p95.
[06:33] Jenna Park: good to know. for SLA language, do you have p95 guarantees on Dedicated?
[06:38] Maya Thompson: yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets based on chosen config and commit level — we'll include SLA language in the docs.
[06:46] Lena Ortiz: about multi-region failover — if we have users in EU and NA, can routing keep them in-region with fallbacks?
[06:51] Carlos Vega: yes — smart routing by region is supported and we can set fallback policies to other regions or lower-capacity model variants.
[06:58] Jenna Park: any suggested initial config for us to hit p95 first-token <150ms at 8 concurrent streaming sessions for a 7B fine-tuned model?
[07:05] Carlos Vega: start with Dedicated small pool of 4 A100 sized GPUs (or equivalent A2x) depending on model ops, int8 quantization, small batch sizes, enable prefix caching and streaming optimizations; our config doc will have more exacts. We'll prototype on a single GPU with warm caches to validate first.
[07:22] Maya Thompson: ok, action items recap: we'll send the benchmark template and pricing (Maya), Carlos will draft a suggested Dedicated config and run a smoke benchmark once we have prompts, Jenna to share prompt set and token distribution.
[07:32] Jenna Park: sounds good. can we also get your SOC2 and VPC checklist?
[07:36] Maya Thompson: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and VPC network checklist to the follow-up.
[07:40] Ravi Menon: and we want to run the benchmark in a test window next week — is that feasible?
[07:44] Carlos Vega: yes, let's aim for next Wed or Thu; I'll coordinate timing and expected resource usage.
[07:49] Lena Ortiz: thanks, this was helpful.
[07:51] Maya Thompson: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.

[08:00] End of recording
